request.description: Train the current PPO baseline with the repository's existing 14-20 cm target-radius exposure to produce the first complete candidate artifact for development measurement. Preserve the current observation, task, reward, and runtime semantics unchanged.
request.rationale: The initial decision is whether the campaign's first intervention should broaden official geometry coverage or address a radius-independent stabilization/dynamics/representation bottleneck. No candidate exists yet, so training the current recipe is the necessary prerequisite for a fair research evaluation. The later measurement will test the candidate over the official 6-20 cm range and inspect uninterrupted-hold diagnostics rather than relying on training proxies.

request.description: Evaluate T1:checkpoint-115712 on the held-out research panel of 160 official-distribution episodes, preserving per-episode target radius, angle, minimum and final distance, first reach, longest hold, in-tolerance steps, and hold interruptions.
request.rationale: This directly discriminates the startup frontier. A sharp deficit concentrated below the 14 cm training boundary supports broadening geometry exposure as the first intervention; failures distributed across the 6–20 cm annulus, especially low longest holds or frequent interruptions despite first reach, support stabilization, dynamics, or representation work instead. The selected checkpoint is the strongest nonterminal proxy checkpoint, not assumed optimal solely because it is late in training.

request.reason: This is the only candidate with completed development evidence and is therefore the strongest evidence-backed baseline, although its 65.625% held-out success is far below the 98% goal. Its diagnostic artifact shows the current gap is concentrated in the official inner-radius regime rather than being established as a general hold-controller failure.

request.candidates_and_roles: Best-known: T1:checkpoint-115712, assigned by E1 using T1 and M1. No working or retained candidate. T1 produced a family of checkpoints, but only T1:checkpoint-115712 has completed development evaluation; its late-training proxy rank does not certify superiority over unmeasured checkpoints.
request.cumulative_resource_use: One fresh training operation (T1, requested 120000 steps; actual learning checkpoints through 120832 due rollout rounding), one research evaluation (M1, 160 episodes, seed 4200), and one best-known role assignment (E1). No source changes, laboratory tools, or additional measurements were used.
request.current_goal_gap: The baseline has a large official-distribution gap. The measured failure pattern is dominated by targets below the 14 cm training-radius lower bound: many such episodes never entered the 1 cm tolerance, whereas the outer-radius portion generally reached and completed the hold. A smaller set of episodes entered tolerance and then exited, so stabilization is not eliminated. The gap is not yet separated into coverage, IK-branch/limit geometry, dynamics, or policy-conditioning causes.
request.current_synthesis: Observed facts: T1 trained the existing PPO recipe with 14-20 cm target exposure and produced checkpoints whose training proxy rose to 0.96 by 115712 steps; these proxies are exposure-limited and are not development performance. M1 evaluated the complete T1:checkpoint-115712 artifact on 160 held-out official-distribution episodes and recorded 65.625% success. Its preserved diagnostics show repeated inner-radius failures with first_reach_step null and minimum distances well outside tolerance, alongside successful inner-radius episodes; some reached episodes show hold interruptions, but uninterrupted completion is common when the target is reached. E1 therefore assigns this candidate as best-known only because it is the sole measured candidate, not because it is near the goal. Interpretation: the strongest current explanation is an exposure/geometry mismatch between 14-20 cm training and the official 6-14 cm folded-arm regime. This is supported by the radius-linked reach failures and by the model's prediction that the official annulus is reachable. A consequential alternative is stabilization or policy conditioning: interruption cases demonstrate that reaching is not sufficient, and the observation may not be used robustly in folded configurations. Branch selection, joint-limit margin, Jacobian conditioning, effective inertia, actuator authority, and intersample motion were not measured by M1, so no causal claim about those mechanisms is established. The candidate comparison is single-artifact evidence; it establishes the tested baseline behavior, not that coverage expansion alone will solve the task or that dynamics are irrelevant.
request.decision_frontier: The unresolved scientific distinction is whether full official-radius exposure is the highest-leverage route to the 98% goal, versus a radius-independent stabilization/representation/dynamics bottleneck that would make coverage expansion insufficient. Evidence that would redirect away from a coverage-first inquiry is a full-radius-trained candidate that still fails broadly across 6-20 cm, or whose failures are predominantly post-entry hold interruptions with adequate reach. Evidence supporting coverage-first work is a reproducible improvement concentrated below 14 cm while outer-radius behavior remains stable. Within any residual inner-radius failures, branch- and limit-conditioned diagnostics plus velocity/action and substep distance are needed before attributing them to IK branch geometry, dynamic authority, or sampled-hold effects.
request.human_goal_connection: The human goal is at least 98% success on the official 6-20 cm, full-angle distribution with an uninterrupted 2-second hold. T1:checkpoint-115712 achieved 105/160 = 65.625% on a held-out development panel, so the campaign remains 32.375 percentage points below the goal and requires a substantial improvement in official-distribution robustness.
request.next_direction_or_closure: Complete startup and enter goal review with a coverage-first proposal, not an intervention claim. Prefer opening one bounded inquiry that compares a full 6-20 cm exposure recipe against the measured baseline using complete candidate evaluations on held-out panels, while preserving the existing hold diagnostics and adding branch/limit or dynamic diagnostics only where needed to explain residual failures. Do not request official assessment: the only measured candidate is 65.625%, far below 98%.
request.next_question: At the next goal review, should the campaign open a bounded inquiry testing whether training exposure expanded to the full official 6-20 cm radius range improves uninterrupted held-out success toward 98%, while measuring whether residual failures are branch/geometry reach failures or post-entry stabilization failures?

request.closure_condition: Close when a full-radius-trained candidate and the measured baseline have comparable held-out evaluation evidence on a non-overlapping panel, including radius-stratified success and preserved first-entry, hold-interruption, velocity/action, branch/limit, and intersample-distance diagnostics where available. A reproducible improvement concentrated below 14 cm with stable outer-radius behavior supports coverage-oriented continuation; little or no improvement, broad-radius degradation, or predominantly post-entry failures redirects the next decision toward the implicated stabilization, representation, dynamics, or geometry mechanism. An implementation or diagnostic limitation may yield a limited or inconclusive closure while preserving the unresolved distinction.
request.goal_connection: The only measured candidate succeeds on 105/160 held-out official-distribution episodes (65.625%), with the largest observed deficit below the 14 cm training lower bound. A full-radius candidate could directly reduce that gap, and matched held-out diagnostics can determine whether remaining failures are reach/geometry failures or interruptions after entry. The result will choose between continuing coverage-oriented development and redirecting effort toward stabilization, representation, dynamics, or geometry.
request.question: Does training the existing PPO implementation with target-radius exposure expanded from 14–20 cm to the full official 6–20 cm range produce a materially higher uninterrupted held-out success rate toward the 98% goal, while failure diagnostics distinguish residual branch/geometry reach failures from post-entry stabilization failures?
request.rationale: The measured baseline is substantially below goal and is the sole evaluated candidate, so official assessment would terminate the campaign on weak evidence. The radius-linked failures make full-radius exposure the highest-value bounded candidate test, but successful reaches followed by hold interruptions and unmeasured branch/dynamic quantities are consequential counterevidence. This inquiry tests the complete changed artifact against the existing measured baseline and preserves diagnostics needed to avoid over-attributing any improvement to coverage alone.
